extracted.intended_audience: Khan Academy software engineers and contributors (developers contributing to the repository)
extracted.subtask_description: A README style guide for code used across Khan Academy projects: sets high-level principles (readability, consistency, prioritization), TODO conventions, and points to per-language style guides. Intended to guide contributors and reviewers in writing and reviewing code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: We implement a style guide for our code with the intention of keeping things readable and consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep code readable and consistent across the codebase; this is the primary intention of the style guide and a general measure of code quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team responsibility to maintain consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do your part on the team to help keep the spirit of this consistency in both your own code, as well as politely pointing out violations in other people's code when doing their code reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should both follow the guide in their own changes and raise style issues in reviews in a polite, constructive manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize shipping and user-visible changes over prettiness
rubrics_metrics.description: While code prettiness should never be valued over launching or any user-visible impacting changes to the code,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let strict stylistic concerns block releases or important user-facing work; balance style enforcement with pragmatic delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintainability through readable code
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining a readable codebase helps things be more maintainable, and in the long run will make it easier to do the real changes that do make user-visible changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor practices that improve long-term maintainability even if they add short-term effort; readability is justified by lower future cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be consistent with surrounding code when editing legacy files
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be lots of legacy files that do not adhere to the current style guide; if you're editing an old file, be consistent with what's around you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modifying legacy files, follow the prevailing conventions in that file rather than wholesale reformatting to the newest style in the same change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tools to automatically catch/fix style violations
rubrics_metrics.description: To help adhere to these rules, some tools are available to automatically catch, and in some cases fix, style violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ linters/formatters and other automatic tooling where available; consult the per-language guides for tool-specific recommendations and configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TODO formatting convention
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is something that you want to deal with later, it’s appropriate to mark it in code. There’s an advantage to using a standard format, which is this: # TODO(your_username): Fix this to work with frobnozzes too # TODO(your_username): Remove this once we support quxxes (at least by Dec 2012)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact TODO format with your username in parentheses so others know who to talk to. The username signals the most knowledgeable person, not an obligation to complete the TODO. You may include scope or rough timing (e.g., 'at least by Dec 2012').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TODOs in code reviews for non-blocking suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: In code reviews, it is common to put in TODOs when a reviewer points out some thing in the code that could be improved, but is not necessary to do right away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a requested change is not required for correctness or release, annotate it as a TODO (using the standard format) rather than blocking the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow per-language style guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Language Style Guides: JavaScript, React, CSS, Python, Go, Java, ObjC (hosted separately) iOS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult and follow the language-specific guides linked in the repository for detailed rules, idioms, and tooling for each language/platform.
